newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cash rates, swaps softer in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek cash rates, swaps softer in late trade.

text.p: Greek money rates were slightly softer following a firm start and forex forwards were trading lower in the short-end of the yield curve while Monday's FRN auction produced an average price slightly above par.
"Depos and forex forwards dipped in afternoon dealing with one week deals around 13.00 from 13.10-13.20 in early trade. One month funds also came down a bit," a money market dealer said.

He said the auction of seven-year floaters drained 325 billion drachmas taking into account the 30 percent of non-competitive bids that was accepted and the central bank maintained its 12.40 percent overnight bid.

Greece auctioned 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 14 percent on Monday, October 21. The average price was a touch above par, 100.001475. The minimum accepted price was 99.9211, the highest 100.25.
The spread is held constant at 150 basis points but the benchmark 12-month T-bill is slashed by 20 basis points to 12.50 percent. The latest one-year T-bill rate was 12.70 percent.

The treasury reserved the right to accept non-competitive bids up to 30 percent of the auctioned amount, it said. It also reserved the right not to accept all or some of the competitive bids that will be submitted.
The mark was quoted at 156.25/30 drachmas from Monday's 156.270 fix, the dollar at 240.23/33 drachmas from 241.050 and the Ecu at 300.24/34 from 300.340 drachmas.
"There were sales of ecu, marks and dollars at the fixing to get into floaters, resulting in a drachma inflow," a trader said.
